source.text: אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא אֶל־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים בְּטֶ֛רֶם יַכֶּ֥ה פַרְעֹ֖ה אֶת־עַזָּֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [That] which came [the] word of Yahweh to Jeremiah the prophet concerning [the] Philistines, before struck Pharaoh Gaza.

en.L: That which came [as] the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza:
en.B: This message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to the prophet Jeremiah about the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza:
en.R: This is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah the prophet about the Philistines. He gave it before Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, attacked the city of Gaza.

es.L: Lo que vino [como] palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} a Jeremías el profeta acerca de los filisteos, antes de que el faraón hiriera a Gaza:
es.B: Este mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino al profeta Jeremías acerca de los filisteos, antes de que el faraón atacara a Gaza:
es.R: Este es el mensaje que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio al profeta Jeremías acerca de los filisteos. Se lo dio antes de que el faraón, rey de Egipto, atacara la ciudad de Gaza.

fr.L: Ce qui fut [comme] parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} adressée à Jérémie le prophète, au sujet des Philistins, avant que le pharaon ne frappe Gaza :
fr.B: Ce message {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressé au prophète Jérémie au sujet des Philistins, avant que le pharaon ne frappe Gaza :
fr.R: Voici le message que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné au prophète Jérémie au sujet des Philistins. Il l’a donné avant que le pharaon, le roi d’Égypte, n’attaque la ville de Gaza.

sw.L: Lile lililokuja [kama] neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa Yeremia nabii juu ya Wafilisti, kabla Farao hajaipiga Gaza:
sw.B: Ujumbe huu kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ulimjia nabii Yeremia kuhusu Wafilisti, kabla Farao hajaipiga Gaza:
sw.R: Huu ndio ujumbe ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimpa nabii Yeremia kuhusu Wafilisti. Alimpa kabla Farao, mfalme wa Misri, hajaushambulia mji wa Gaza.

vi.L: Điều đã đến [là] lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} với nhà tiên tri Giê-rê-mi về người Phi-li-tin, trước khi Pha-ra-ôn đánh Ga-xa:
vi.B: Sứ điệp này từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với nhà tiên tri Giê-rê-mi về người Phi-li-tin, trước khi Pha-ra-ôn đánh Ga-xa:
vi.R: Đây là sứ điệp {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho nhà tiên tri Giê-rê-mi về người Phi-li-tin. Ngài ban sứ điệp này trước khi Pha-ra-ôn, vua Ai Cập, tấn công thành Ga-xa.

ko.L: 바로가 가사를 치기 전에, 블레셋 사람들에 관하여 예언자 예레미야에게 임한 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이다.
ko.B: 바로가 가사를 치기 전에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 블레셋 사람들에 관하여 예언자 예레미야에게 주신 말씀이다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 블레셋 사람들에 관하여 예언자 예레미야에게 주신 말씀은 이러하다. 그분께서는 이집트 왕 바로가 가사 성을 공격하기 전에 이 말씀을 주셨다.

pt.L: Aquilo que veio [como] a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} a Jeremias, o profeta, a respeito dos filisteus, antes que Faraó ferisse Gaza:
pt.B: A palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} que veio ao profeta Jeremias a respeito dos filisteus, antes que Faraó atacasse Gaza:
pt.R: Esta é a mensagem que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} deu ao profeta Jeremias a respeito dos filisteus. Ele a deu antes que Faraó, o rei do Egito, atacasse a cidade de Gaza.

decisions.choice: a heading for the oracle against the Philistines
decisions.reason: The verse opens with "which", the same heading form Jeremiah uses for the drought poems (14:1) and for other oracles against the nations (46:1; 49:34). It names the people the message is about, the Philistines, who lived in the cities of the southern coastal plain (25:20).

decisions.choice: a Pharaoh of Egypt who attacked Gaza; which one is not stated
decisions.reason: The verse dates the oracle by an Egyptian attack on Gaza, the southernmost Philistine city, but does not name the king. The likeliest is Necho II, who marched up the coast in 609 BC on his way to the Euphrates (2 Kings 23:29) and fought the Babylonians near the border of Egypt around 601 BC; either campaign could have brought him against Gaza. An earlier or later Pharaoh cannot be ruled out. The date only fixes when the word came: the danger the poem describes comes from the north (verse 2), not from Egypt.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew heading, with Jeremiah's name and the date
decisions.reason: In the Greek translation, where this oracle stands as chapter 29 (see the note at 1:1), the heading is much shorter: it says only that the oracle is about the Philistines (the Greek calls them "the foreigners") and lacks the mention of Jeremiah and of Pharaoh's attack on Gaza. This is written from general knowledge. The Hebrew is followed here.

decisions.choice: That which came [as] the word of the LORD ... / This message from the LORD came to the prophet Jeremiah ... / This is the message the LORD gave Jeremiah ...
decisions.reason: The heading follows the wording used for the same form at 14:1, which adapts the settled formula "the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD" to this order. Balanced and Readable say "message" as that formula does, and Balanced makes the heading a sentence, as 46:1 does.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh, the king of Egypt ... the city of Gaza
decisions.reason: Readable says who Pharaoh was and that Gaza was a city, for readers who do not know the names, and splits the heading into two sentences.

decisions.choice: Lo que vino [como] palabra del SEÑOR (L); Este mensaje del SEÑOR vino (B); Este es el mensaje que el SEÑOR le dio (R)
decisions.reason: The heading of the oracles against the nations, as in 46:1.

decisions.choice: The heading of the oracles against the nations as at 46:1
decisions.reason: One wording for each heading in chapters 46-51.

decisions.choice: Aquilo que veio [como] a palavra do SENHOR (L); A palavra do SENHOR que veio (B); Esta é a mensagem que o SENHOR deu (R)
decisions.reason: The heading has the form of 14:1 and 46:1 (m1) and keeps their Portuguese at each level; "Gaza", "Ascalom", "Tiro" and "Sidom" are the forms 25:20-22 gives these cities.

source.text: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנֵּה־מַ֜יִם עֹלִ֤ים מִצָּפוֹן֙ וְהָיוּ֙ לְנַ֣חַל שׁוֹטֵ֔ף וְיִשְׁטְפוּ֙ אֶ֣רֶץ וּמְלוֹאָ֔הּ עִ֖יר וְיֹ֣שְׁבֵי בָ֑הּ וְזָֽעֲקוּ֙ הָֽאָדָ֔ם וְהֵילִ֕ל כֹּ֖ל יוֹשֵׁ֥ב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: look, waters [are] rising from [the] north, and they will become a torrent overflowing, and they will overflow [the] land and its fullness, [the] city and [those] dwelling in it; and will cry out the people, and will wail every inhabitant of the land.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, waters [are] rising from the north, \q and they will become an overflowing torrent; \q they will overflow the land and all that fills it, \q the city and those who live in it. \q And the people will cry out, \q and every inhabitant of the land will wail.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: See, waters are rising in the north; \q they will become a torrent in flood \q and sweep over the land and everything in it, \q the city and all who live there. \q People will cry out, \q and everyone who lives in the land will wail.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Look! Water is rising in the north. \q It will become a river in flood. \q It will cover the land and everything in it, \q the cities and the people who live in them. \q People will scream for help. \q Everyone in the land will cry out in grief.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: He aquí, suben aguas del norte, \q y se convertirán en torrente desbordado; \q inundarán la tierra y su plenitud, \q la ciudad y a los que habitan en ella. \q Y clamarán los hombres, \q y gemirá todo habitante de la tierra.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: He aquí que suben las aguas en el norte; \q se convertirán en un torrente desbordado \q que arrasará la tierra y todo lo que hay en ella, \q la ciudad y a todos los que viven allí. \q La gente gritará, \q y gemirán todos los habitantes del país.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: ¡Atención! El agua está subiendo en el norte. \q Se convertirá en un río desbordado. \q Cubrirá la tierra y todo lo que hay en ella, \q las ciudades y a la gente que vive en ellas. \q La gente gritará pidiendo ayuda. \q Todos en el país llorarán de dolor.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Voici, des eaux montent du nord, \q et elles deviendront un torrent qui déborde ; \q elles submergeront le pays et ce qui le remplit, \q la ville et ceux qui l’habitent. \q Et les hommes crieront, \q et tous les habitants du pays se lamenteront.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Voyez, des eaux montent au nord ; \q elles deviendront un torrent en crue \q et submergeront le pays et tout ce qu’il contient, \q la ville et tous ceux qui l’habitent. \q Les gens pousseront des cris, \q et tous les habitants du pays se lamenteront.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Regardez ! L’eau monte au nord. \q Elle va devenir un fleuve en crue. \q Elle couvrira le pays et tout ce qu’il contient, \q les villes et les gens qui y habitent. \q Les gens hurleront pour appeler au secours. \q Tous les habitants du pays pleureront de chagrin.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Tazama, maji [yanapanda] kutoka kaskazini, \q nayo yatakuwa mto unaofurika; \q yataifurikia nchi na vyote vilivyomo, \q mji na wale wakaao ndani yake. \q Na watu watalia, \q na kila mkaaji wa nchi ataomboleza.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Tazama, maji yanapanda upande wa kaskazini; \q yatakuwa mto uliofurika \q na kuifunika nchi na kila kitu kilichomo, \q mji na wote wanaoishi humo. \q Watu watalia, \q na kila mtu anayeishi katika nchi ataomboleza.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Tazama! Maji yanapanda huko kaskazini. \q Yatakuwa mto wenye mafuriko. \q Yataifunika nchi na kila kitu kilichomo, \q miji na watu wanaoishi ndani yake. \q Watu watapiga kelele kuomba msaada. \q Kila mtu katika nchi atalia kwa huzuni.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: Này, nước dâng lên từ phương bắc, \q sẽ thành dòng thác tràn ngập; \q chúng sẽ tràn ngập xứ và mọi vật trong xứ, \q thành và những kẻ ở trong thành. \q Người ta sẽ kêu la, \q và mọi dân cư trong xứ sẽ than khóc.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: Kìa, nước đang dâng lên ở phương bắc; \q chúng sẽ thành dòng thác lũ \q tràn qua xứ và mọi vật trong xứ, \q tràn qua thành và mọi người sống ở đó. \q Người ta sẽ kêu la, \q mọi người sống trong xứ sẽ than khóc.
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Hãy xem! Nước đang dâng lên ở phương bắc. \q Nước sẽ thành một dòng sông lũ lụt. \q Nước sẽ phủ khắp xứ và mọi vật trong xứ, \q phủ các thành và những người sống trong đó. \q Người ta sẽ kêu cứu. \q Mọi người trong xứ sẽ khóc than đau đớn.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 보라, 북쪽에서 물이 불어 올라 \q 넘쳐흐르는 급류가 되어, \q 땅과 그 안에 가득한 것과 \q 성읍과 그 안에 사는 자들을 덮을 것이다. \q 사람들이 부르짖고, \q 그 땅의 모든 주민이 울부짖을 것이다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 보라, 북쪽에서 물이 불어 올라 \q 범람하는 급류가 되어, \q 땅과 그 안에 있는 모든 것과 \q 성읍과 그 주민들을 휩쓸 것이다. \q 사람들이 부르짖고, \q 그 땅에 사는 모든 사람이 울부짖을 것이다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 보아라! 북쪽에서 물이 불어 오르고 있다. \q 그 물이 홍수 난 강이 될 것이다. \q 그 물이 땅과 그 안에 있는 모든 것을 덮을 것이다. \q 성읍들과 거기 사는 사람들을 덮을 것이다. \q 사람들이 살려 달라고 소리칠 것이다. \q 그 땅에 사는 모든 사람이 슬피 울 것이다.

pt.L: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Eis que águas sobem do norte, \q e se tornarão uma torrente transbordante; \q inundarão a terra e tudo o que a enche, \q a cidade e os que nela habitam. \q E as pessoas gritarão, \q e todo morador da terra uivará.
pt.B: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Vejam, águas estão subindo no norte; \q vão se tornar uma torrente em cheia \q e cobrirão a terra e tudo o que há nela, \q a cidade e todos os que moram ali. \q As pessoas vão gritar, \q e todos os que moram na terra vão se lamentar aos gritos.
pt.R: É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz: Olhem! A água está subindo no norte. \q Vai virar um rio em cheia. \q Vai cobrir a terra e tudo o que há nela, \q as cidades e as pessoas que moram nelas. \q As pessoas vão gritar por socorro. \q Todos na terra vão chorar de tristeza.

decisions.choice: waters from the north: an invading army pictured as a flood
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's enemy from the north is Babylon (1:14-15; 6:22; 25:9), and the oracle against Egypt pictures the same army rising like the Nile (46:7-8, 20). Isaiah uses the same picture for Assyria, a river overflowing its banks and sweeping through the land (Isaiah 8:7-8). Verse 3 turns from the picture to the horses and chariots it stands for.

decisions.choice: the land and its fullness: the land and everything in it
decisions.reason: "Its fullness" means all that fills the land, its people, animals and goods (8:16; Psalm 24:1). "City" is singular but stands for every town, as the next line's "every inhabitant" shows.

decisions.choice: the verbs after "look" speak of what is about to happen
decisions.reason: The waters are already rising (a participle); the verbs that follow describe what they will do next: flood the land, and the people cry out.

decisions.choice: people ... wail / scream for help ... cry out in grief
decisions.reason: The word for "people" here means human beings in general and needs no gender setting. Readable says "cry out in grief" for the verb of wailing, as Isaiah's Readable does, and makes "cry out" a scream for help, the sense of this verb (Judges 6:6-7).

decisions.choice: the cities and the people who live in them
decisions.reason: Readable makes the collective singular "city" plural so that it is not read as one particular town (m2).

decisions.choice: "Ainsi parle le SEIGNEUR :" (L); "Le SEIGNEUR dit ceci :" (B); "Voici ce que dit le SEIGNEUR :" (R)
decisions.reason: The messenger formula as the French terms note sets it, followed by a colon and no quotation marks in the oracles.

decisions.choice: nước dâng lên từ phương bắc
decisions.reason: The invading army is pictured as a flood; Vietnamese keeps the picture at every level, as the English does.

source.text: מִקּ֗וֹל שַֽׁעֲטַת֙ פַּרְס֣וֹת אַבִּירָ֔יו מֵרַ֣עַשׁ לְרִכְבּ֔וֹ הֲמ֖וֹן גַּלְגִּלָּ֑יו לֹֽא־הִפְנ֤וּ אָבוֹת֙ אֶל־בָּנִ֔ים מֵֽרִפְי֖וֹן יָדָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: From [the] sound of [the] stamping of [the] hooves of his mighty [ones], from [the] rattling of his chariotry, [the] rumbling of his wheels, not have turned fathers to children from slackness of hands,

en.L: At the sound of the stamping of the hooves of his stallions, \q at the rattling of his chariots, the rumbling of his wheels, \q fathers have not turned back to [their] {{gender:children|sons}} \q because of the slackness of [their] hands,
en.B: At the sound of his stallions' hooves pounding, \q at the clatter of his chariots and the rumble of their wheels, \q fathers do not turn back for their {{gender:children|sons}}; \q their hands hang limp,
en.R: The enemy's war horses pound the ground with their hooves. \q His chariots rattle and their wheels roar. \q When people hear it, fathers do not even turn back for their {{gender:children|sons}}. \q They are too weak with fear to help them.

es.L: Al ruido del golpear de los cascos de sus corceles, \q al estruendo de sus carros, al estrépito de sus ruedas, \q los padres no se vuelven hacia [sus] hijos \q por la flojedad de [sus] manos,
es.B: Al oír el golpeteo de los cascos de sus corceles, \q el estruendo de sus carros y el estrépito de sus ruedas, \q los padres no se vuelven por sus hijos; \q sus manos cuelgan sin fuerza,
es.R: Los caballos de guerra del enemigo golpean el suelo con sus cascos. \q Sus carros hacen estruendo y sus ruedas retumban. \q Cuando la gente lo oye, los padres ni siquiera se vuelven para buscar a sus hijos. \q El miedo los deja sin fuerzas para ayudarlos.

fr.L: Au bruit du martèlement des sabots de ses étalons, \q au fracas de ses chars, au grondement de ses roues, \q les pères ne se sont pas retournés vers [leurs] {{gender:enfants|fils}}, \q à cause de la faiblesse de [leurs] mains,
fr.B: Au bruit des sabots de ses étalons qui martèlent le sol, \q au fracas de ses chars et au grondement de leurs roues, \q les pères ne se retournent pas pour leurs {{gender:enfants|fils}} ; \q leurs mains pendent sans force,
fr.R: Les chevaux de guerre de l’ennemi frappent le sol de leurs sabots. \q Ses chars font un bruit de tonnerre et leurs roues grondent. \q En les entendant, les pères ne se retournent même pas pour leurs {{gender:enfants|fils}}. \q Ils ont trop peur pour avoir la force de les aider.

sw.L: Kwa sauti ya kishindo cha kwato za farasi wake hodari, \q kwa mshindo wa magari yake ya vita, mvumo wa magurudumu yake, \q baba hawakugeuka nyuma kwa ajili ya wana [wao] \q kwa sababu ya kulegea kwa mikono [yao],
sw.B: Kwa sauti ya kwato za farasi wake hodari zinazodunda, \q kwa mshindo wa magari yake ya vita na mvumo wa magurudumu yake, \q baba hawageuki nyuma kwa ajili ya watoto wao; \q mikono yao imelegea,
sw.R: Farasi wa vita wa adui wanaipiga ardhi kwa kwato zao. \q Magari yake ya vita yanatoa mshindo, na magurudumu yake yananguruma. \q Watu wanaposikia, akina baba hawageuki hata kuwachukua watoto wao. \q Wameishiwa nguvu kwa hofu, hawawezi kuwasaidia.

vi.L: Nghe tiếng vó chiến mã của nó dậm, \q tiếng xe chiến của nó rầm rập, tiếng bánh xe nó ầm ầm, \q các người cha không quay lại [cứu] con cái mình, \q vì tay [họ] rã rời,
vi.B: Nghe tiếng vó chiến mã của nó dồn dập, \q tiếng xe chiến của nó rầm rập và bánh xe ầm ầm, \q các người cha không quay lại cứu con cái mình; \q tay họ buông thõng,
vi.R: Ngựa chiến của quân thù giậm vó rầm rập. \q Xe chiến của nó rầm rầm, bánh xe ầm ầm. \q Khi nghe tiếng ấy, các người cha thậm chí không quay lại tìm con cái mình. \q Họ sợ đến rụng rời, không còn sức để cứu con.

ko.L: 그의 군마들의 발굽이 땅을 구르는 소리와 \q 그의 병거들이 덜컹거리는 소리와 그 바퀴들이 요란한 소리 때문에, \q 아버지들이 [자기] {{gender:자녀들|아들들}}을 돌아보지 못한다. \q [그들의] 손에 힘이 빠졌기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그의 군마들이 발굽으로 땅을 구르는 소리와 \q 병거들이 덜컹거리고 바퀴들이 요란하게 구르는 소리에, \q 아버지들은 {{gender:자녀들|아들들}}을 돌아보지도 못한다. \q 손에 힘이 다 빠져 버렸다.
ko.R: 원수의 군마들이 발굽으로 땅을 쿵쿵 구른다. \q 그의 병거들이 덜컹거리고 바퀴들이 요란하게 구른다. \q 그 소리를 들은 아버지들은 {{gender:자녀들|아들들}}을 돌아보지도 않고 달아난다. \q 그들은 너무 무서워서 자녀들을 도울 힘이 없다.

pt.L: Ao som do bater dos cascos dos seus garanhões, \q ao estrondo dos seus carros, ao ruído das suas rodas, \q os pais não se voltaram para [os seus] filhos \q por causa da fraqueza [das suas] mãos,
pt.B: Ao som dos cascos dos seus garanhões batendo no chão, \q ao estrondo dos seus carros e ao ruído das suas rodas, \q os pais não voltam para buscar os filhos; \q as suas mãos ficam sem força,
pt.R: Os cavalos de guerra do inimigo batem os cascos no chão. \q Os seus carros fazem estrondo, e as rodas fazem barulho. \q Quando as pessoas ouvem isso, os pais nem voltam para buscar os filhos. \q Estão fracos demais de medo para ajudá-los.

decisions.choice: his mighty ones: his stallions, the enemy's war horses
decisions.reason: The word means "mighty ones" and is used for powerful horses (8:16; 50:11). Here the stamping of their hooves is what is heard.

decisions.choice: "his": the invader, not named
decisions.reason: The horses, chariots and wheels belong to "him", the enemy from the north of verse 2, spoken of as one man. He is never named in the poem.

decisions.choice: slackness of hands: strength gone from fear
decisions.reason: Hands that hang loose are a picture of people so terrified that they cannot act (6:24; 50:43; Isaiah 13:7; Ezekiel 7:17). The fathers are so overcome that they run without stopping for their children.

decisions.choice: have not turned: what is coming is described as if it were already seen
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form used for completed action, but it belongs to the coming invasion of verse 2: the prophet describes the scene as if he were watching it. The sentence runs on into verse 4, which gives the reason.

decisions.choice: children (alternative: sons)
decisions.reason: The word is the plural of "son", but in a flight from an invading army it means sons and daughters alike, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: The enemy's war horses ... When people hear it ... too weak with fear to help them
decisions.reason: Readable names the enemy as the owner of the horses (m2), says what the sounds do to the people, and explains the picture of slack hands (m3). It ends the sentence here; verse 4 begins a new one.

decisions.choice: hijos
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" already includes daughters, so the English gender setting needs no span here.

decisions.choice: "wana" (L), "watoto" (B, R), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: "Wana" and "watoto" already include daughters, so there is no second wording for the setting to offer.

decisions.choice: con cái
decisions.reason: "Sons" here means the children; Vietnamese "con cái" covers both, so no gender span is used where the English has one.

decisions.choice: "{{gender:자녀들|아들들}}" at every level
decisions.reason: As the English setting at every level here; Korean has two real wordings.

decisions.choice: os filhos, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English puts "children" under the gender setting, since sons and daughters alike are meant. Portuguese "filhos" already includes daughters, as the Old Testament terms set it (and 6:21; 13:14), so no setting is needed.

source.text: עַל־הַיּ֗וֹם הַבָּא֙ לִשְׁד֣וֹד אֶת־כָּל־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים לְהַכְרִ֤ית לְצֹר֙ וּלְצִיד֔וֹן כֹּ֖ל שָׂרִ֣יד עֹזֵ֑ר כִּֽי־שֹׁדֵ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים שְׁאֵרִ֖ית אִ֥י כַפְתּֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: because of the day the coming to destroy all [the] Philistines, to cut off to Tyre and to Sidon every survivor helping; for [is] destroying Yahweh [the] Philistines, [the] remnant of [the] coastland of Caphtor.

en.L: because of the day that is coming to destroy all the Philistines, \q to cut off from Tyre and from Sidon \q every surviving helper; \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is destroying the Philistines, \q the remnant of the coastland of Caphtor.
en.B: because the day is coming to destroy all the Philistines \q and to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every ally they have left. \q For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is destroying the Philistines, \q what is left of the coastland of Caphtor.
en.R: That is because the day is coming to destroy all the Philistines. \q It will cut off the last of those who could help the cities of Tyre and Sidon. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is destroying the Philistines, \q the last of the people who came from the island of Crete.

es.L: a causa del día que viene para destruir a todos los filisteos, \q para cortar de Tiro y de Sidón \q a todo aliado que quede; \q porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} destruye a los filisteos, \q al remanente de la costa de Caftor.
es.B: porque llega el día de destruir a todos los filisteos \q y de cortar de Tiro y de Sidón a todo aliado que les quede. \q Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está destruyendo a los filisteos, \q lo que queda de la costa de Caftor.
es.R: Esto es porque llega el día de destruir a todos los filisteos. \q Acabará con los últimos que podían ayudar a las ciudades de Tiro y Sidón. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está destruyendo a los filisteos, \q los últimos del pueblo que vino de la isla de Creta.

fr.L: à cause du jour qui vient pour détruire tous les Philistins, \q pour retrancher de Tyr et de Sidon \q tout allié qui reste ; \q car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} détruit les Philistins, \q le reste de l’île de Caphtor.
fr.B: car le jour vient où tous les Philistins seront détruits \q et où Tyr et Sidon perdront le dernier allié qui leur restait. \q Car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} détruit les Philistins, \q ce qui reste de l’île de Caphtor.
fr.R: C’est que le jour arrive où tous les Philistins seront détruits. \q Les villes de Tyr et de Sidon perdront les derniers qui auraient pu les aider. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} détruit les Philistins, \q les derniers du peuple venu de l’île de Crète.

sw.L: kwa sababu ya siku ile inayokuja kuwaangamiza Wafilisti wote, \q kukatilia mbali kutoka Tiro na kutoka Sidoni \q kila msaidizi aliyesalia; \q kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anawaangamiza Wafilisti, \q mabaki ya pwani ya Kaftori.
sw.B: kwa sababu siku inakuja ya kuwaangamiza Wafilisti wote, \q na kuwakatilia mbali Tiro na Sidoni kila mshirika aliyewabakia. \q Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anawaangamiza Wafilisti, \q mabaki ya pwani ya Kaftori.
sw.R: Hiyo ni kwa sababu siku inakuja ya kuwaangamiza Wafilisti wote. \q Itawakatilia mbali watu wa mwisho ambao wangeweza kuisaidia miji ya Tiro na Sidoni. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anawaangamiza Wafilisti, \q watu wa mwisho waliotoka katika kisiwa cha Krete.

vi.L: vì ngày đang đến để hủy diệt mọi người Phi-li-tin, \q để diệt trừ khỏi Ty-rơ và Si-đôn \q mọi kẻ giúp đỡ còn sót lại; \q vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang hủy diệt người Phi-li-tin, \q là những người sót lại của miền duyên hải Cáp-tô.
vi.B: vì ngày đang đến để hủy diệt mọi người Phi-li-tin \q và cắt đứt khỏi Ty-rơ và Si-đôn mọi đồng minh còn lại. \q Vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang hủy diệt người Phi-li-tin, \q là những người còn lại của miền duyên hải Cáp-tô.
vi.R: Đó là vì ngày đang đến để hủy diệt mọi người Phi-li-tin. \q Ngày ấy sẽ cắt đứt những người cuối cùng có thể giúp các thành Ty-rơ và Si-đôn. \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang hủy diệt người Phi-li-tin, \q là những người cuối cùng thuộc dân đã đến từ đảo Cơ-rết.

ko.L: 모든 블레셋 사람을 멸망시킬 날, \q 두로와 시돈에게서 \q 살아남은 돕는 자를 모두 끊어 버릴 날이 오기 때문이다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 블레셋 사람들, \q 곧 갑돌 섬에 남은 자들을 멸망시키신다.
ko.B: 모든 블레셋 사람을 멸망시킬 날이 오고, \q 두로와 시돈에게 남은 동맹군을 모두 끊어 버릴 날이 오기 때문이다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 블레셋 사람들, \q 곧 갑돌 바닷가 땅에서 남은 자들을 멸망시키신다.
ko.R: 모든 블레셋 사람을 멸망시킬 날이 다가오고 있기 때문이다. \q 그날에 두로 성과 시돈 성을 도울 마지막 사람들까지 끊어질 것이다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 블레셋 사람들을 멸망시키신다. \q 그들은 크레타 섬에서 온 사람들 가운데 마지막 남은 자들이다.

pt.L: por causa do dia que vem para destruir todos os filisteus, \q para eliminar de Tiro e de Sidom \q todo ajudador que restar; \q pois {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} está destruindo os filisteus, \q o remanescente da costa de Caftor.
pt.B: porque está chegando o dia de destruir todos os filisteus \q e de eliminar todo aliado que ainda resta a Tiro e Sidom. \q Pois {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} está destruindo os filisteus, \q o que restou da costa de Caftor.
pt.R: Isso acontece porque está chegando o dia de destruir todos os filisteus. \q Esse dia vai acabar com os últimos que podiam ajudar as cidades de Tiro e Sidom. \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} está destruindo os filisteus, \q os últimos do povo que veio da ilha de Creta.

decisions.choice: because of the day: the reason the fathers flee
decisions.reason: The verse continues verse 3: the fathers run without their children because the day of destruction has come. "The day" is a fixed time of judgment, here the day the LORD has set for the Philistines (46:10).

decisions.choice: every helper left to Tyre and Sidon: the allies of the Phoenician cities
alternatives: every survivor from Tyre and Sidon who comes to help
decisions.reason: Tyre and Sidon were the great trading cities on the coast north of Israel, and they are named with the Philistines elsewhere (25:22; 27:3; Joel 4:4). The Hebrew says the day will cut off "for Tyre and Sidon" every helper who survives: with the Philistines gone, those cities have no ally left to come to their aid. It could also mean that any survivor from Tyre and Sidon who came to help the Philistines will be cut off; the sense is the same, no help will be left.

decisions.choice: the coastland of Caphtor: most likely the island of Crete, where the Philistines came from
alternatives: Cappadocia or another coast of Asia Minor
decisions.reason: The Philistines came from Caphtor (Amos 9:7; Deuteronomy 2:23; compare Genesis 10:14). Caphtor is most likely Crete, which Egyptian records call by a similar name, and some Philistines were called Cherethites, "Cretans" (Ezekiel 25:16; Zephaniah 2:5). The Greek translation of the Old Testament renders Caphtor elsewhere as Cappadocia, in Asia Minor (this is written from general knowledge). "The remnant of the coastland of Caphtor" means the last of the people who came from there.

decisions.choice: the LORD is the destroyer
decisions.reason: The same verb, "destroy", is used twice: the day comes to destroy the Philistines, and it is the LORD who is destroying them. The army from the north does the work, but the poem names the LORD as the one acting (verses 6-7).

decisions.choice: every ally they have left
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "surviving helper" as "ally", the role the helper plays in war (m2).

decisions.choice: the last of the people who came from the island of Crete
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely modern name of Caphtor (m3), as Isaiah's Readable says "Cyprus" for Kittim, and says the Philistines came from there. It begins a new sentence, since verse 3 ended one.

decisions.choice: la costa de Caftor (L, B); la isla de Creta (R)
decisions.reason: Caphtor is most likely Crete, where the Philistines came from (Amos 9:7); Readable names it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "pwani ya Kaftori" (L, B); "kisiwa cha Krete" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Readable names Caphtor by its likely modern name, Crete, the spelling of Acts 27.

decisions.choice: đảo Cơ-rết (R); Cáp-tô (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable names Caphtor by its likely place, the island of Crete, as the English Readable does; Cơ-rết is the published form of Acts 27.

decisions.choice: "갑돌 섬" (L), "갑돌 바닷가 땅" (B); "크레타 섬" (R)
decisions.reason: Caphtor keeps its biblical name at Literal and Balanced; Readable names the island as the English does.

source.text: בָּ֤אָה קָרְחָה֙ אֶל־עַזָּ֔ה נִדְמְתָ֥ה אַשְׁקְל֖וֹן שְׁאֵרִ֣ית עִמְקָ֑ם עַד־מָתַ֖י תִּתְגּוֹדָֽדִי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Has come baldness to Gaza; is silenced Ashkelon, [the] remnant of their valley; until when will you gash yourself?

en.L: Baldness has come upon Gaza; \q Ashkelon is silenced, the remnant of their valley. \q How long will you gash yourself?
en.B: Gaza has shaved its head in mourning; \q Ashkelon is silenced, the remnant of their valley. \q How long will you gash yourself?
en.R: The people of Gaza have shaved their heads in grief. \q Ashkelon is silent, and so are the last people of the Philistine plain. \q How long will you cut yourselves in sorrow?

es.L: Ha venido la calvicie sobre Gaza; \q Ascalón ha sido silenciada, el remanente de su valle. \q ¿Hasta cuándo te harás cortes?
es.B: Gaza se ha rapado la cabeza en señal de duelo; \q Ascalón ha quedado en silencio, el resto de su valle. \q ¿Hasta cuándo te harás cortes?
es.R: La gente de Gaza se ha rapado la cabeza de tristeza. \q Ascalón está en silencio, y también los últimos habitantes de la llanura de los filisteos. \q ¿Hasta cuándo {{plural_you:se harán|os haréis}} cortes de dolor?

fr.L: La calvitie est venue sur Gaza ; \q Ashqelôn est réduite au silence, le reste de leur vallée. \q Jusqu’à quand te feras-tu des incisions ?
fr.B: Gaza s’est rasé la tête en signe de deuil ; \q Ashqelôn est réduite au silence, le reste de leur vallée. \q Jusqu’à quand te feras-tu des incisions ?
fr.R: Les habitants de Gaza se sont rasé la tête de chagrin. \q Ashqelôn se tait, et les derniers habitants de la plaine des Philistins aussi. \q Jusqu’à quand vous ferez-vous des entailles en signe de deuil ?

sw.L: Upara umeijia Gaza; \q Ashkeloni imenyamazishwa, mabaki ya bonde lao. \q Hata lini utajikatakata?
sw.B: Gaza imenyoa kichwa chake kwa maombolezo; \q Ashkeloni imenyamazishwa, mabaki ya bonde lao. \q Hata lini utajikatakata?
sw.R: Watu wa Gaza wamenyoa vichwa vyao kwa huzuni. \q Ashkeloni iko kimya, nao watu wa mwisho wa tambarare ya Wafilisti vilevile. \q Mtajikata miili yenu kwa huzuni mpaka lini?

vi.L: Ga-xa đã bị cạo trọc đầu; \q Ách-ca-lôn bị làm cho câm lặng, là những kẻ sót lại trong thung lũng của chúng. \q Ngươi sẽ rạch mình cho đến bao giờ?
vi.B: Ga-xa đã cạo trọc đầu để tang; \q Ách-ca-lôn bị làm cho câm lặng, là những kẻ sót lại trong thung lũng của chúng. \q Ngươi còn rạch mình cho đến bao giờ?
vi.R: Dân Ga-xa đã cạo trọc đầu vì đau buồn. \q Ách-ca-lôn im lặng, những người cuối cùng của đồng bằng Phi-li-tin cũng vậy. \q Các ngươi còn rạch mình than khóc cho đến bao giờ?

ko.L: 가사에 대머리가 닥쳤고, \q 아스글론, 그들의 골짜기에 남은 자가 잠잠해졌다. \q 너는 언제까지 네 몸에 상처를 내겠느냐?
ko.B: 가사는 슬퍼서 머리를 밀었고, \q 아스글론, 그들의 골짜기에 남은 자가 잠잠해졌다. \q 너는 언제까지 네 몸에 상처를 내려느냐?
ko.R: 가사 백성은 슬퍼서 머리를 밀었다. \q 아스글론도 잠잠하고, 블레셋 평야에 마지막 남은 사람들도 잠잠하다. \q 너희는 언제까지 슬퍼하며 몸에 상처를 내려느냐?

pt.L: A calvície veio sobre Gaza; \q Ascalom foi silenciada, o remanescente do vale deles. \q Até quando farás cortes em ti mesma?
pt.B: Gaza raspou a cabeça em sinal de luto; \q Ascalom foi silenciada, o que restou do vale deles. \q Até quando farás cortes em ti mesma?
pt.R: O povo de Gaza raspou a cabeça de tristeza. \q Ascalom está em silêncio, e também os últimos moradores da planície dos filisteus. \q Até quando vocês vão se cortar de tanta dor?

decisions.choice: baldness has come to Gaza: Gaza mourns
decisions.reason: Shaving the head was a sign of mourning for the dead and for disaster (16:6; 48:37; Isaiah 15:2; Micah 1:16). The city is pictured as a mourner with a shaved head.

decisions.choice: silenced: brought to silence, which may mean destroyed
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "be silent" or "be cut off, be destroyed" (Hosea 10:7, 15; Zephaniah 1:11). Both fit: Ashkelon is struck dumb with grief, or it is wiped out and falls silent. "Silenced" keeps something of both.

decisions.choice: the remnant of their valley
decisions.reason: "Valley" here would be the low coastal plain where the Philistine cities stood, and "their" refers to the Philistines. The Greek translation reads "the remnant of the Anakim", the race of giants who survived in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod (Joshua 11:22), which reflects a Hebrew word spelled almost the same; a related word in other Semitic languages means "strength", which would give "the remnant of their strength". These readings are written from general knowledge. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: how long will you gash yourself: cutting the body in mourning
decisions.reason: Cutting the skin was a mourning rite among Israel's neighbors and sometimes in Judah (16:6; 41:5; 48:37), though the law forbade it to Israel (Deuteronomy 14:1; Leviticus 19:28). The verb is feminine singular: the speaker turns to the mourning city or remnant, perhaps Ashkelon, and asks how long the grief will go on.

decisions.choice: has shaved its head in mourning / have shaved their heads in grief
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the baldness is (m1). Readable speaks of the people of Gaza and of the mourners in the plural, and adds "in sorrow" to show why they cut themselves (m4).

decisions.choice: the last people of the Philistine plain
decisions.reason: Readable says "plain" for the low land along the coast, which a reader may not think of as a valley, and names the Philistines for "their" (m3).

decisions.choice: farás cortes em ti mesma (tu, feminine)
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine singular (m4): the city is addressed as a mourning woman, with "tu" and the feminine "mesma"; Readable speaks to the mourners as "vocês", as the English Readable turns to the people in the plural.

source.text: ה֗וֹי חֶ֚רֶב לַֽיהוָ֔ה עַד־אָ֖נָה לֹ֣א תִשְׁקֹ֑טִי הֵאָֽסְפִי֙ אַל־תַּעְרֵ֔ךְ הֵרָגְעִ֖י וָדֹֽמִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: Ah, sword of Yahweh, until where not will you be quiet? Gather yourself into your sheath; rest and be still.

en.L: Ah, sword of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q how long will you not be quiet? \q Gather yourself into your sheath; \q rest and be still.
en.B: Ah, sword of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q how long before you are quiet? \q Go back into your sheath; \q rest and be still.
en.R: Oh, sword of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q When will you stop? \q Go back into your sheath. \q Rest there and be still.

es.L: ¡Ay, espada {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! \q ¿Hasta cuándo no te aquietarás? \q Vuélvete a tu vaina; \q reposa y quédate quieta.
es.B: ¡Ay, espada {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! \q ¿Cuánto falta para que te calmes? \q Vuelve a tu vaina; \q descansa y quédate quieta.
es.R: ¡Oh, espada {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! \q ¿Cuándo te vas a detener? \q Vuelve a tu vaina. \q Descansa allí y quédate quieta.

fr.L: Ah ! épée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q jusqu’à quand ne te reposeras-tu pas ? \q Rentre dans ton fourreau ; \q arrête-toi et tiens-toi tranquille.
fr.B: Ah ! épée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q combien de temps encore avant que tu te reposes ? \q Rentre dans ton fourreau ; \q arrête-toi et reste tranquille.
fr.R: Oh ! épée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ! \q Quand vas-tu t’arrêter ? \q Rentre dans ton fourreau. \q Repose-toi et reste tranquille.

sw.L: Aha, upanga wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q hata lini hutatulia? \q Jikusanye katika ala yako; \q pumzika, utulie.
sw.B: Aha, upanga wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q utatulia lini? \q Rudi katika ala yako; \q pumzika, utulie.
sw.R: Lo, upanga wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! \q Utaacha lini? \q Rudi katika ala yako. \q Pumzika humo, utulie.

vi.L: Ôi, gươm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q cho đến bao giờ ngươi mới yên lặng? \q Hãy thu mình vào vỏ; \q hãy nghỉ ngơi và nằm yên.
vi.B: Ôi, gươm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q bao giờ ngươi mới chịu yên? \q Hãy trở vào vỏ; \q hãy nghỉ ngơi và nằm yên.
vi.R: Ôi, gươm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}! \q Bao giờ ngươi mới thôi? \q Hãy trở vào vỏ. \q Hãy nằm yên trong đó.

ko.L: 아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 칼아, \q 언제까지 네가 잠잠하지 않으려느냐? \q 네 칼집으로 들어가 \q 쉬고 가만히 있어라.
ko.B: 아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 칼아, \q 언제쯤에야 네가 잠잠하겠느냐? \q 네 칼집으로 돌아가 \q 쉬면서 가만히 있어라.
ko.R: 오, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 칼아! \q 언제 멈추겠느냐? \q 칼집으로 돌아가거라. \q 거기서 쉬며 가만히 있어라.

pt.L: Ah, espada {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, \q até quando não ficarás quieta? \q Recolhe-te à tua bainha; \q descansa e fica em silêncio.
pt.B: Ah, espada {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, \q quanto tempo falta para ficares quieta? \q Volta para a tua bainha; \q descansa e fica parada.
pt.R: Ah, espada {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}! \q Quando vais parar? \q Volta para a tua bainha. \q Descansa ali e fica parada.

decisions.choice: ah: an anguished cry calling on the sword, not a threat against it
decisions.reason: The cry often announces doom on someone (22:13; 23:1), but it can also be a cry of grief or a call for attention (30:7; Isaiah 55:1). Here it is a plea addressed to the sword: the speaker does not threaten the sword but begs it to stop.

decisions.choice: the sword of the LORD: the LORD's judgment carried out in war
decisions.reason: The LORD's sword is the slaughter of war sent as his judgment (12:12; 46:10; Isaiah 34:5-6; Deuteronomy 32:41-42). The sword is spoken to as a living thing, as Ezekiel speaks to it (Ezekiel 21:21).

decisions.choice: the speaker is not named
decisions.reason: The plea may be the prophet's or the cry of the stricken Philistines; the poem does not say. Verse 7 answers it: the sword cannot rest because the LORD has sent it. As elsewhere in Jeremiah's poetry, the voices are not marked with quotation marks.

decisions.choice: until where: how long
decisions.reason: "Until where" is a way of asking "how long" (Exodus 16:28; Psalm 13:2).

decisions.choice: Ah / Oh
decisions.reason: The terms for this book render this cry "Woe" ("Woe to ..."; Readable "How terrible it will be for ..."). Here that would say that disaster is coming on the sword, the opposite of the sense (m1), so this verse departs from it, as Isaiah 55:1 does. Reviewers may prefer "Alas".

decisions.choice: ¡Ay! (L, B); ¡Oh! (R)
decisions.reason: *Hoy* in a plea, as set in the terms note.

decisions.choice: "Aha" (L, B); "Lo" (R)
decisions.reason: An anguished cry calling on the sword, not a threat; Swahili "Ole" would turn it into a woe.
*Hoy* here is a plea to the sword, not a threat: "Ah" as the French terms note sets for a plea.

decisions.choice: Ôi
decisions.reason: The cry *hoy* as a plea, as the terms note sets it for this verse: "Ôi" at every level.

decisions.choice: "아" (L, B); "오" (R) for *hoy* as a plea
decisions.reason: The Jeremiah note: in a plea *hoy* is "Ah" / "Oh", not a woe.

decisions.choice: Ah
decisions.reason: The cry here is a plea to the sword, not doom on it (m1), so Portuguese says "Ah", as the English says "Ah"; "Ai" ("Ai de ...") would turn it into a woe on the sword. The sword is spoken to with "tu".

source.text: אֵ֣יךְ תִּשְׁקֹ֔טִי וַֽיהוָ֖ה צִוָּה־לָ֑הּ אֶֽל־אַשְׁקְל֛וֹן וְאֶל־ח֥וֹף הַיָּ֖ם שָׁ֥ם יְעָדָֽהּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: How will you be quiet, and Yahweh has commanded it against Ashkelon and against [the] shore of the sea? There he has appointed it.

en.L: How can you be quiet, \q when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded it? \q Against Ashkelon and against the shore of the sea, there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has appointed it.
en.B: But how can you be quiet \q when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given you orders? \q Against Ashkelon and the seacoast, there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent you.
en.R: But how can you rest? \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has given you orders. \q He has sent you to attack Ashkelon and the land along the sea.

es.L: ¿Cómo te aquietarás, \q si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te ha dado orden? \q Contra Ascalón y contra la costa del mar, allí {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} la ha destinado.
es.B: Pero ¿cómo podrás calmarte \q si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te ha dado órdenes? \q Contra Ascalón y la costa del mar, allí te ha enviado.
es.R: Pero ¿cómo vas a descansar? \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te ha dado órdenes. \q Te ha enviado a atacar a Ascalón y la tierra junto al mar.

fr.L: Comment te reposerais-tu, \q quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a donné un ordre ? \q Contre Ashqelôn et contre le rivage de la mer, c’est là qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a assignée.
fr.B: Mais comment pourrais-tu te reposer \q quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a donné des ordres ? \q Contre Ashqelôn et la côte de la mer, c’est là qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} t’a envoyée.
fr.R: Mais comment pourrais-tu te reposer ? \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a donné des ordres. \q Il t’a envoyée attaquer Ashqelôn et le pays au bord de la mer.

sw.L: Utawezaje kutulia, \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekuamuru? \q Juu ya Ashkeloni na juu ya pwani ya bahari, huko ndiko alikouweka.
sw.B: Lakini utawezaje kutulia \q wakati {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekupa amri? \q Juu ya Ashkeloni na pwani ya bahari, huko ndiko alikokutuma.
sw.R: Lakini utawezaje kupumzika? \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekupa amri. \q Amekutuma kuishambulia Ashkeloni na nchi iliyo kando ya bahari.

vi.L: Làm sao ngươi yên lặng được, \q khi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền lệnh cho nó? \q Nghịch cùng Ách-ca-lôn và nghịch cùng bờ biển, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chỉ định nó ở đó.
vi.B: Nhưng làm sao ngươi yên được \q khi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ra lệnh cho ngươi? \q Ngài đã sai ngươi đến đánh Ách-ca-lôn và miền bờ biển.
vi.R: Nhưng làm sao ngươi nghỉ được? \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ra lệnh cho ngươi. \q Ngài đã sai ngươi đến tấn công Ách-ca-lôn và miền dọc bờ biển.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그것에 명령하셨는데, \q 그것이 어찌 잠잠할 수 있겠느냐? \q 아스글론과 바닷가를 치라고 그분께서 거기에 그것을 정해 두셨다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너에게 명령하셨는데, \q 네가 어찌 잠잠할 수 있겠느냐? \q 그분께서 아스글론과 바닷가를 치라고 너를 보내셨다.
ko.R: 그러나 네가 어떻게 쉴 수 있겠느냐? \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너에게 명령을 내리셨다. \q 그분께서 아스글론과 바닷가 땅을 치라고 너를 보내셨다.

pt.L: Como ficarás quieta, \q se {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} lhe deu ordem? \q Contra Ascalom e contra a costa do mar, ali {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} a designou.
pt.B: Mas como poderás ficar quieta, \q se {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} te deu ordens? \q Contra Ascalom e contra o litoral, ali {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} te enviou.
pt.R: Mas como podes descansar? \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} te deu ordens. \q Ele te enviou para atacar Ascalom e a terra junto ao mar.

decisions.choice: the answer to the plea, still spoken to the sword
decisions.reason: The question "how can you be quiet?" answers verse 6 with the same verb: the sword cannot rest. In the next words the speaker turns from speaking to the sword ("you") to speaking about it ("it"). The Greek translation reads "how will it be quiet" throughout (written from general knowledge); the Hebrew keeps "you" in the question.

decisions.choice: commanded ... appointed: the LORD has given the sword its task and its place
decisions.reason: The second verb means to set a time or place by appointment (Micah 6:9; 2 Samuel 20:5). The sword has been given orders and told where to strike, and it cannot stop until it has done so.

decisions.choice: Ashkelon and the shore of the sea: the Philistine coast
decisions.reason: Ashkelon was the Philistine port on the Mediterranean coast; "the shore of the sea" is the coastal strip where the Philistine cities lay (Ezekiel 25:16; Zephaniah 2:5-7).

decisions.choice: has given you orders ... has sent you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep speaking to the sword as "you" through the verse, since English would stumble on the change of person (m1). Literal keeps "it". They add "But" to show that this answers verse 6. Readable says "attack" for the sense of "against".
